extra.message: User-controlled fileName, arg1, and arg2 are concatenated directly into a shell command string and executed via child_process.exec() without any escaping or validation. These values originate from the request URL (path, item, price) in routes/php.js, allowing arbitrary command injection (e.g., ?item=x;ls).

User-controlled values extracted from request.originalUrl (queryParams.path, queryParams.item, queryParams.price) are passed as fileName and command arguments to execPHP.parseFile, which interpolates them into a shell command executed with child_process.exec(). This is the source of command injection.

result.path is taken directly from the request path (query.split("?")[0]) with no validation and later used as the file name in execphp.js where it is prefixed with ./phpFiles/. An attacker can supply a path such as /../../etc/passwd.php to traverse the filesystem and execute arbitrary PHP files or read arbitrary files.

libxml_disable_entity_loader(false) re-enables external entity loading, and DOMDocument::loadXML is called with LIBXML_NOENT | LIBXML_DTDLOAD on XML that embeds user-controlled $argv[1]/$argv[2] (the item/price query parameters from routes/php.js) without escaping. This allows XXE, e.g., reading file:///etc/passwd (the $malicious payload in this file demonstrates the intended attack).

req.body.username and req.body.password are passed directly into a MongoDB findOne query. Because express.urlencoded({ extended: true }) and express.json() parse nested objects, an attacker can submit username[$ne]=x&password[$ne]=x to bypass authentication (the query matches any user).
req.body.username is used directly in a MongoDB findOne filter. With extended body parsing, an object like {"$ne": ""} can be injected to alter the query semantics (operator injection).

The /admin management page is exposed with no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can access the admin interface and the administrative APIs (user list, add user, delete user).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /users/userlist returns all user records with no authentication or authorization check, exposing every user's data (including password and credit card) to unauthenticated callers.

extra.message: DELETE /users/deleteuser/:id takes an arbitrary id from the URL and deletes that user record with no authentication or authorization. Any caller can delete any user (IDOR / broken access control).

extra.message: collection.find({}, {}) returns and res.json(docs) serializes entire user documents, exposing sensitive fields including password (stored in plaintext) and credit card number to any caller.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is hardcoded ("Shh, its a secret!"). An attacker who knows the secret can forge session cookies and impersonate arbitrary users.

User-controlled database fields (this.username, this.email, this._id) are concatenated into HTML strings without escaping and injected via $('.userList table tbody').html(tableContent). Since these values originate from unauthenticated user input (POST /users/adduser), this is a stored/DOM XSS vulnerability.

Session is configured with saveUninitialized: true, resave: true, and no cookie.secure or cookie.sameSite attributes. This permits session cookies to be transmitted over HTTP and makes CSRF/session-fixation attacks easier.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: No X-Frame-Options header or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive is set anywhere in the application, leaving the site vulnerable to clickjacking (the repository even ships a clickjacking/ demo).
